subject: Burst window saturation — immediate mitigation & procurement path for EmberPay
messages:
From: Alyssa Park <alyssa.park@emberpay.com>
To: lukas_meyer@redwood.com
Cc: support@emberpay.com
Date: Sun, 1 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Production latency + 5xx burst during 08:30–09:00 PST window

Lukas — we hit a sustained latency and error spike this morning during our morning settlement window (approx 08:30–09:00 PST).

Symptoms: 
- 95th percentile token latency jumped from ~180ms to ~850ms for generation API.
- ~6% 5xx rate for streaming responses; retrying clients saw throttles and higher tail latencies.
- Our telemetry shows queue depth spike correlating with a high-concurrency batch of invoice generation jobs.

We are on a reserved capacity plan (EMB-2025-42) and expected headroom for the morning window. This is material for us — if this persists we will need to postpone customer settlements.

I've attached a trimmed ops log with request IDs and timestamps. Can you confirm whether this is isolated to our Dedicated pool or a broader scheduling/autoscale regression? Also, we need to understand options for short-term burst capacity while we evaluate longer-term committed capacity changes.

[Attachment: emberpay_ops_log_1101.csv (24KB)]

— Alyssa
Alyssa Park
Head of Payments Ops, EmberPay
alyssa.park@emberpay.com

From: lukas_meyer@redwood.com
To: Alyssa Park <alyssa.park@emberpay.com>
Cc: monica_patel@redwood.com, marcus_lin@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 1 Nov 2026 09:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production latency + 5xx burst during 08:30–09:00 PST window

Alyssa — thanks for the heads up and the log. I'm investigating now. Initial notes: 
- I've opened an ops ticket and attached the log to our internal bridge.
- We're seeing queueing on the Embery-dedicated pool that matches your timestamps; early signal points to contention from a heavy KV-cache warmup and a high token-count batch job.

Immediate actions I'm kicking off: 
1) Prioritize EmberPay traffic on the affected pool for the next 2 hours to reduce tail latency.
2) Enable a temporary model-variant fallback (smaller quantized variant) for non-critical invoice generation to reduce per-token GPU time.
3) Requesting a 2-hour burst credit allocation from capacity to cover peak load while we root-cause.

I'll keep you updated within 30 minutes on whether the prioritization and fallback cut the 95th down. Monica & Marcus — tagging you for customer comms and any procurement/credit requests.

Thanks,
Lukas Meyer
Account Exec — Priority Accounts
Redwood Inference
From: lukas_meyer@redwood.com
To: hannah_schmitt@redwood.com, marcus_lin@redwood.com, monica_patel@redwood.com, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 1 Nov 2026 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Production latency + 5xx burst during 08:30–09:00 PST window

Team — forwarding EmberPay alert. TL;DR: reserved pool that should have headroom experienced saturation during their morning settlement burst; customer is sensitive (settlements). Need rapid decision on:

- Short-term: approve 2 hours of burst capacity + immediate priority routing and model fallback (operational, low risk).
- Medium-term: discuss increasing reserved commit or adjusting autoscale policy for EmberPay's deterministic window.
- Commercial: EmberPay will ask for a goodwill credit if we cannot demonstrate immediate relief.

Operational detail summary (ops findings so far):
- Scheduled job between 08:28–08:45 with many long contexts causing KV-cache warmups and reduced batch efficiency.
- Fallback to a quantized variant is expected to reduce per-token GPU time by ~35% but needs approval because it slightly impacts output quality for a subset of prompts.

Requested approvals:
- Hannah: greenlight up to $X of burst credits (please confirm number below).
- Vivek: ops sign-off on changing priority routing + model fallback for EmberPay while we triage.

Attachments: emberpay_ops_log_1101.csv, proposed_burst_plan_v2.pdf

Thanks — Lukas

From: hannah_schmitt@redwood.com
To: lukas_meyer@redwood.com, marcus_lin@redwood.com, monica_patel@redwood.com, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 1 Nov 2026 11:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Production latency + 5xx burst during 08:30–09:00 PST window

Lukas / team — I approve the short-term measures: prioritization, model-variant fallback, and up to 2 hours of burst credits (approve $7k equivalent). Please pursue these now and capture timelines and customer-facing language.

Vivek — please confirm ETA for routing change and whether we need a hotfix to autoscaler. If this is a scheduling logic regression, we should mark SEV and consider a rollback window.

Marcus / Monica — draft a short customer note offering the following: 
- Immediate mitigation steps (what we did)
- Offer one settlement-cycle credit if we miss SLA again in the next 30 days
- Proposed follow-up: a sizing review + optional reserved commit increase to lock in headroom for the morning window.

Hannah Schmitt
Head of Sales Operations
Redwood Inference

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Alyssa Park <alyssa.park@emberpay.com>, lukas_meyer@redwood.com, monica_patel@redwood.com
Cc: hannah_schmitt@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 2 Nov 2026 15:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Burst window saturation — immediate mitigation & procurement path for EmberPay

Alyssa — quick update and next steps after today's validation window: 

What we did (summary): 
- Prioritized EmberPay requests on the dedicated pool for 10:00–12:00 PST (reduced 95th from ~850ms to ~240ms).
- Enabled quantized model variant for non-customer-facing invoice rendering jobs (reduced GPU time; small quality delta verified by Monica).
- Allocated a 2-hour burst credit to cover the immediate impact (applied to today's invoice settlement run).

Evidence: attached trimmed ops log and the proposed mitigation plan we executed.

Recommendations (recommended next steps): 
1) Scheduling tweak: move heavy batch warmups out of the 08:15–09:00 window if possible — we'll provide suggested windows that preserve latency headroom.
2) Procurement: consider a 15% reserved commit uplift for morning windows or adopt a scheduled uplift policy for deterministic peak windows. We can run a cost/latency trade-off analysis with your engineering team.
3) Follow-up: 48-hour post-mortem with ops + engineering; we'll share root-cause analysis and a timeline for any autoscale fixes.

We appreciate the quick signal — Monica will coordinate a short call to walk through the plan and the uplift options later today. Please reply with availability.

Attachments: proposed_burst_plan_v2.pdf, emberpay_ops_log_1101.csv

— Marcus Lin
Account Lead, Priority Accounts
Redwood Inference
